title: Shared conformance fixtures for Apache Iceberg implementations
summary: Neelesh Salian, Sung Yun and Andrei Tserakhau merged two earlier threads into one proposal: a standalone, language-neutral repository of conformance fixtures modelled on parquet-testing, starting with static inputs paired with the value the spec fixes (type strings, transforms) and growing to binary fixtures. There is no harness or central gate; each implementation pins the repository and asserts in its own test suite, with Java and Go first, covering v2 and v3. Proofs of concept exist for PyIceberg, iceberg-rust and iceberg-go. After a community sync, open items were the repository name and verifying both reads and writes. Andrei supported the read-first corpus, favoured the name iceberg-verification, and argued that write verification matters because many divergences are write bugs; he described an engine-free prototype that runs a logical operation log through each implementation and compares a canonical form, with a demo matrix over Go, Rust and Java. A dedicated sync was scheduled for August 19th 2026.

positions.stance: Create a shared, language-neutral fixtures repository with no harness or central gate, starting from the smallest primitives and with Java and Go first.

Supports the read-first corpus and the name iceberg-verification, and argues write verification through an engine-agnostic operation log should follow because many cross-implementation bugs are in what writers produce.

outcome.note: The proposal is still under review; repository naming and read-versus-write verification were raised at the community sync, and a dedicated sync was set for 2026-08-19.

why_it_matters: If adopted, every Iceberg implementation would test its reading of the spec against the same fixtures instead of only against itself.
